AI_MONTESSORI_ANALYST.purpose: Analyze child's weekly progress like a master Montessorian, detect sensitive periods, identify concerns, recommend next works

research_insights.observation_method: Document objectively: what happens, not interpretation. Track work selection, duration, repetitions, completion, transitions.
normalization_markers: Love of work (intrinsic motivation, maximum effort)

repetition_meaning.productive: Deep concentration + calm + joy + increasing precision = SENSITIVE PERIOD ACTIVE
repetition_meaning.concerning: Distracted + agitated + no improvement = wrong difficulty or anxiety

research_insights.mastery_test: Three Period Lesson - Period 3 (recall without prompting) = true mastery

order.signs: tantrums over routine changes, notices tiny environmental changes, insists on sequences

language.signs: vocabulary explosion, asks 'what's that?', fascinated by letters

movement.signs: constant physical activity, practices same movement repeatedly

sensory.signs: touches everything, sorts by sensory attribute

small_objects.signs: collects tiny treasures, points out minute details

social.signs: mimics adult social behaviors, watches peer interactions

reading.signs: points to letters, asks 'what does that say?'

math.signs: counts spontaneously, asks 'how many?', notices patterns

recommendation_scoring.interest_alignment: 40 points - work area matches recent interests
recommendation_scoring.sensitive_period_match: 35 points - work matches active sensitive period
recommendation_scoring.curriculum_sequence: 25 points - next logical step in progression

TRACING_FLEET_AUDIT_2026_09_03.status: SHIPPED — fixed build_tracing_booklet.py so each per-spread trace page traces the literal last word of THAT spread's own reader page, not the book hero word; all 16 sat-cast tracing workbooks rebuilt, fleet-audited (16/16 clean, zero defects), republished, MD5-verified 16/16 live; STORYBOOK_PRINT_VERSION 27 -> 28; commit be44f64f3
TRACING_FLEET_AUDIT_2026_09_03.rule: Word-mode tracing pages trace spread_trace_word(sp) — the literal last word of that spread's own text (punctuation stripped, lowercased; last element if text is a list) — falling back to the book's hero word (book['new']) only for a spread with no text at all. This means a book's trace pages are not all one word: the-nap traces 'naps' on character pages but 'nap' on the potato page; the-cot's finale traces 'naps'; the-kit's and the-bug's finale trace 'potato'; the-dog's finale traces 'dogs' — all confirmed correct against the real reader PDFs, not just books_def.py.
TRACING_FLEET_AUDIT_2026_09_03.root_cause: Word mode previously always traced book['new'] (the book's hero word) on every spread regardless of what that spread's own reader page actually said — wrong for the minority of spreads with a different last word (plurals, alternate finale nouns).
TRACING_FLEET_AUDIT_2026_09_03.code_change: scripts/curriculum/flashcards/build_tracing_booklet.py: added spread_trace_word(sp); build_trace_booklet()'s trace_text_page() now computes page_word = spread_trace_word(sp) or word per spread and sizes it against the same book-wide x-height ceiling (word_ceiling = book_word_xheight(book)) via compute_trace_u(page_word, ceiling=word_ceiling).
